description: Single-panel engineering stress–strain plot for Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel, SLM-printed at five laser powers plus the as-cast condition. The ordinate is labelled "Engineering Stress/MPa" (0–1200, gridlines every 200) and the abscissa "Engineer Strain/%" (0–60, gridlines every 10); the legend at lower right lists six curves as P-70 (black), P-90 (red), P-110 (blue), P-130 (green), P-150 (purple) and as-cast (orange). All five SLM curves show a steep elastic rise followed by a long, nearly flat plastic plateau lying above the 1000 MPa gridline, and each ends in an abrupt vertical drop signalling fracture without necking-type softening. The orange as-cast curve is clearly the weakest: it plateaus between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines and terminates just past the 20% strain gridline. The blue P-110 curve lies highest over most of the strain range and extends furthest, beyond the 50% gridline. No numeric data labels are printed on any curve; only axis ticks carry numbers, so the panel demonstrates qualitatively that SLM processing raises both strength and ductility above the as-cast state, with ~110 W appearing optimal.

observations.observation: Axes are labelled "Engineering Stress/MPa" (0–1200, ticks every 200) and "Engineer Strain/%" (0–60, ticks every 10), with light gridlines.
The legend contains exactly six entries in the order P-70 (black), P-90 (red), P-110 (blue), P-130 (green), P-150 (purple), as-cast (orange).
The as-cast (orange) curve has the lowest plateau, lying between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines, and fractures just after the 20% strain gridline.
All five SLM curves reach a plateau above the 1000 MPa gridline and end in abrupt vertical drops at different strains, indicating fracture without pronounced post-necking softening.
The blue curve (legend P-110) attains the highest plateau stress and the largest fracture strain, extending beyond the 50% strain gridline.
No numerical values are printed on the curves themselves; the only numbers in the image are the axis ticks and legend labels.
The caption identifies the figure as tensile stress–strain curves of Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloys SLM printed at various laser powers together with the as-cast Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy.
Citing text states the P-70 sample (laser power 70 W) had yield strength 776.9 MPa, tensile strength 986.4 MPa and elongation 23.10%.
Citing text states a laser power of 110 W (P-110) gave the best mechanical properties: yield strength 887.1 MPa, tensile strength 1076.8 MPa and elongation 40.80%.
Citing text states properties deteriorate above 110 W, with yield strength, tensile strength and elongation decreasing to 771.5 MPa, 1032.0 MPa and 28.28% at 150 W.
Citing text attributes the higher strength and plasticity of SLM samples over the cast sample to grain-refinement strengthening from rapid cooling during SLM.
Citing text states the yield-strength, tensile-strength and fracture-strain values of these curves are tabulated in Table 2, which is not part of this figure.

Because several curves overlap, the individual endpoint (fracture) strain of each coloured curve cannot be assigned to its legend label with certainty from the pixels alone; only the as-cast and blue curves are unambiguous.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa, 0–1200) versus engineer strain (%, 0–60) plot with six curves: P-70 (black), P-90 (red), P-110 (blue), P-130 (green), P-150 (purple) and as-cast (orange). All SLM curves plateau above 1000 MPa and end in sharp vertical fracture drops; the as-cast curve plateaus between 800 and 900 MPa and ends just past 20% strain.

unreadable_items: Individual fracture points (stress/strain at the vertical drop) of each curve are unlabelled and partly overlapping, so per-curve fracture strains cannot be read off the plot
